items.title: The truncation of a path type is the path type of the truncation, for every truncation level

items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled theorem at source lines 671-674 (book Theorem 7.3.12): for every A, x, y : A and n \ge -2 the map of equation eq:path-trunc-map is an equivalence, so \trunc n{x=_A y} is equivalent to the path type of \trunc{n+1}A between the two projections. The statement records only that equivalence, while the proof (source lines 676-722) has to run the encode-decode method in full: it generalises the two endpoints to arbitrary elements of \trunc{n+1}A through a family P whose very well-definedness is an application of the level result thm:hleveln-of-hlevelSn, defines decode on the generators and justifies that by n-truncatedness of the codomain, builds r by induction on the truncation, defines encode by transporting r along the given path, and then verifies both composites: the first reduces by path induction to an equation whose goal is an (n-1)-type, the second needs the five-step computation that moves the transport of \tproj n{\refl x} along ap(\tproj{n+1})(p) through the truncation and the path family, using thm:transport-compose and thm:ap-transport. There is no way to induct on an equality between two projections, which is exactly why the generalisation is unavoidable.
